item.name: Single-binary cross-platform release pipeline
item.contract: A reproducible CI pipeline produces signed single-binary releases for linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, windows/amd64, and android/arm64 (Termux) on every git tag. Each binary is ≤30 MB, includes version + build metadata, and has its install size and SHA recorded in the release notes. Mirrors install.sh / install.ps1 to fetch the right asset.
item.degraded_mode: Without a release pipeline, the v1.0 differentiator ("single binary on X platforms") cannot be substantiated; users still build from source.
ready_when: Sharp v1.0 differentiator (8.D row 1) is decided.
go build ./cmd/gormes succeeds on all seven target GOOS/GOARCH combinations from CI or a Linux runner where cross-compilation is supported.
All release child rows, including `Termux latest-installer follow-up release publication`, are complete or explicitly superseded by release-lane evidence.
not_ready_when: Binary size exceeds 30 MB for any target without an explicit operator-approved exception.
Termux build is missing or fails CGO-equivalent restrictions.
Release artifacts are unsigned.
The row is assigned as one combined release-pipeline implementation slice instead of a focused child closure.
No tagged-release run has produced and attached all seven artifacts from the current workflow.
The live latest release is still v0.2.20 and the P0 Termux follow-up release publication row is blocked on explicit release-lane approval.
acceptance: TestReleasePipelineMatrix confirms a build for each target produces a single binary ≤30 MB.
TestReleaseBinaryHasVersionMetadata confirms `gormes version` reports the tag, commit, and build date for each platform.

install.sh and install.ps1 select the correct binary for the platform and verify its SHA before exec.

item.name: Release binary version/provenance smoke guard

item.degraded_mode: Without a binary smoke guard, the workflow can inject ldflags and publish archives while never proving the produced executable reports the tag, commit, dirty bit, and build date that release notes and fleet automation rely on.
ready_when: Release build-date provenance injection is complete.
Release archive 30 MB size gate is complete.
The release workflow already builds the seven target archives and can use static workflow fixtures; no tag push or live GitHub release is required.
not_ready_when: The slice publishes a release, pushes a tag, changes version numbers, or requires a live GitHub Actions run.
The workflow only checks source-code variables and never inspects the built binary.
The workflow tries to execute cross-compiled Windows, Android, or non-host-architecture binaries instead of using `go version -m` as a cross-target metadata fallback.
acceptance: TestReleaseWorkflowSmokeChecksBinaryVersionMetadata fails until the build step runs host-compatible binaries with `version --json` and checks `version`, `git_commit`, `git_dirty`, and `build_date` against the release build variables.
The same build step falls back to `go version -m` for cross-compiled targets so every matrix leg has a binary metadata probe without executing incompatible artifacts.
The smoke check runs after `go build` and before `tar -C dist -czf`, `sha256sum`, the archive size gate, SBOM generation, attestations, and artifact upload.

item.name: Release build-date provenance injection
item.contract: The release workflow injects a UTC build timestamp into every prebuilt binary, and `gormes version --json` reports it as build_date beside the semver tag, Hermes-style date alias, git commit, dirty bit, Go runtime, OS, and arch. Developer/source builds may fall back to Go VCS build-info time or `unknown`, but tagged release artifacts must carry the workflow-injected timestamp.
item.degraded_mode: Without build_date, operators can verify the release tag and source commit but cannot tell when a downloaded binary was minted; the parent release pipeline acceptance remains only partially satisfied.
ready_when: Sharp v1.0 differentiator decision is complete.
Release workflow already injects Version, GitCommit, and GitDirty through ldflags.
`gormes version --json` already exposes release provenance fields and is covered by cmd/gormes tests.
not_ready_when: The slice requires a live GitHub release, tag push, or platform matrix build.
The workflow records a local timezone, mutable generated file, or release-note-only timestamp instead of binary-embedded UTC provenance.
The human `gormes version` output is widened with noisy metadata rather than keeping detailed provenance in `--json`.
acceptance: TestVersionCommand_JSONIncludesBuildDateField fails before version JSON includes build_date and passes after the field is always present.
Resolver tests prove ldflags-injected BuildDate wins, VCS build-info time is a fallback, and missing metadata returns `unknown` instead of an empty string.
TestReleaseWorkflowInjectsBuildDateProvenance proves the release workflow computes BUILD_DATE in UTC and passes `-X main.BuildDate=${BUILD_DATE}` in the build ldflags.
Existing release workflow tests for target slugs, SHA-256 sidecars, SBOM generation, size cap, release-note sizes, artifact upload, and tag-only publication remain green.

item.name: Release SBOM attestation binding
item.contract: The release workflow binds each generated SPDX SBOM to its matching release archive through GitHub artifact attestations. After the matrix build creates `dist/gormes-${version}-${goos}-${goarch}.tar.gz` and `dist/gormes-${version}-${goos}-${goarch}.sbom.json`, CI must run the current GitHub SBOM attestation action with the tarball as `subject-path` and the SPDX file as `sbom-path` before upload.
item.degraded_mode: Without an SBOM attestation binding, operators receive SBOM files and build-provenance attestations but cannot verify that the published SPDX document is cryptographically associated with the release archive.

item.name: Release build provenance attest action contract
item.contract: The release workflow binds every matrix-built tar.gz release archive to GitHub build-provenance artifact attestations using the current artifact-attestation action shape: `actions/attest@v4` with the matrix-specific archive as `subject-path`. The attestation must run after the archive, checksum, size gate, and SBOM are produced, before the archive is uploaded from the build job, while preserving SBOM attestation, SHA-256 sidecars, release-note size/SHA output, and installer asset publication.

item.name: Release archive 30 MB size gate
item.contract: The release workflow enforces the v1 differentiator's single 30 MB binary promise before release artifacts are uploaded: every built archive is checked against a 31,457,280-byte cap after packaging and checksum generation, and any oversize archive fails the build with a clear target-specific message.
item.degraded_mode: If an archive exceeds the cap, the release matrix fails before upload or publication; operators keep source-build installs rather than receiving an oversized prebuilt binary.

not_ready_when: The slice requires a live GitHub tag push, real release publication, or changing installer selection logic.

Oversize failures happen after upload-artifact or GitHub release publication.
